title: A marked secret rule ran before PEM redaction in log text, so a key after password= kept its body
resolution: Log text now redacts PEM private keys before the marked secret rules; a logger test covers fields and correlation.

title: Revealed-value spans were replaced before the PEM scan, so a revealed word inside a key marker exposed the key body
resolution: PEM key spans are found in the original text and merged with the revealed spans before replacement; tests cover redactSecrets and redactFailure.

title: A missing installation CA let an initialized installation fall back to a plain broker connection
resolution: A missing CA is allowed only before the installation record exists; otherwise the settings and broker commands fail with the path before connecting, and re-issue still runs.

title: The tracked private key check missed indented YAML keys and JSON-escaped keys such as the authority document
resolution: The check also matches an indented line break and an escaped one; tests use keys generated at run time and keep bare markers in code allowed.

title: The issuer accepted an authority certificate with another authority's key, and re-issue could replace working files
resolution: The adapter refuses an authority that is no CA or does not match its key, and every certificate is issued before any file is written; a test shows the files stay unchanged.

title: The default broker CA was read with readFileSync, outside the namespace's link, owner, and mode checks
resolution: The CA is read through ControlPlaneNamespace; tests refuse a symbolic link, a file readable by others, and another owner.

title: The CertificateIssuer port had no shared conformance suite for its adapters
resolution: CERTIFICATE_ISSUER_CONFORMANCE in @taskelith/fleet takes the issuer and a certificate inspector; the x509 adapter runs it with the Node inspector of @taskelith/testing.

title: verify-installation stopped and started after the re-issue, hiding whether the command itself restarts the services
resolution: Right after the command, a probe compares the certificates the API and NATS present with the new files and a worker heartbeat must arrive; without the restart the check failed.

title: The guide implied that the browser certificate variables work in Compose, which passes and mounts neither
resolution: The guide, the contract, and the local installation delta state that the composition serves the API certificate until 26d and separate the direct start.

title: verification.md named the base before the merge of origin/dev
resolution: The record names the merge c12a7425 and its merge base 3f23516a, what it brought in, and the checks repeated after it.

title: The server certificate ended 397 days after issuance instead of 397 days after its backdated start
resolution: The end is computed from notBefore, and the test asserts the difference of the two ends.

title: Three contracts still said the API and NATS run over plain HTTP and NATS
resolution: The execution wire, account pool, and source control contracts state the TLS of 26a and what 26b and 26d add; pass 3 confirmed it in part, and its source control wording was fixed after pass 3 without review.

title: The served certificate probe ran once right after compose restart, with no wait for the services
resolution: The probe is retried until CONTACT_SECONDS; a service that still serves its old certificate fails at the deadline. A regression of the pass 1 fix of finding 8.

title: The changed G2 scenario code was not run, and the limitations named it incompletely
resolution: Run on a native Ubuntu x86_64 host by Liki at 6a0d8687: full make verify, the G2 suites with services, verify-linux-crash-windows, and verify-linux-cgroup passed; the changed G2 files ran. No review pass checked it.

title: The qualification named a macOS x86_64 host and verification.md an arm64 one
resolution: The qualification names the actual host, macOS 26.6.2 arm64 (Apple M3).

title: The issuer signed with an expired authority or one ending before the server certificate
resolution: Refused with precondition-failed and a note that rollover is G6 work, before any file is written; a conformance case and a delta scenario cover it.

title: A browser key that does not parse or match was reported under TASKELITH_BROWSER_TLS_CERT
resolution: Failures name the certificate or the key, whichever is at fault; the tests expect TASKELITH_BROWSER_TLS_KEY.

title: An API key that does not match its certificate named neither api-key.pem nor the remedy
resolution: The failure names api-key.pem, api-certificate.pem, and make installation-certificates; an integration test swaps the key.

title: The scenario Before initialization read as contradicting Lost installation CA
resolution: Its WHEN names neither an installation record nor an installation CA.

title: The authority requirement did not name the failing commands and kept a sentence allowing plain NATS
resolution: It names init and issue-installation-certificates and refers client CA behavior to the nats-transport requirement.

title: The scenarios Browser certificate in the composition and Plain broker client had no test
resolution: A composition test shows no browser setting or file reaches the control plane; pass 3 confirmed it in part, and the plain client probe was tightened after pass 3 without review.

title: The private key check missed double-escaped and single-line keys and read the working copy
resolution: Both forms are refused, and tracked files are read from the index with git cat-file --batch; tests cover each.

title: The guide's running worker host wording was unclear
resolution: It says running installation.

title: PostgreSQL was said to stay plain on localhost, though the composition does not publish it
resolution: The delta, proposal, guide, and contract say plain on the Compose network, unpublished; the G3 plan's deferral row is unchanged.

title: The plain NATS client probe took any -ERR, such as an authorization refusal, as proof that TLS is required
resolution: Passes only when INFO advertises tls_required and the server closes or sends the TLS required error; fixed without review by the away delegate decision of 2026-10-28 under the three pass cap.

title: The source control contract said the installation has neither ingress nor TLS, then described its HTTPS
resolution: It says the installation has no externally reachable ingress.

title: Remaining gates left out make verify-linux-cgroup, which Limitations lists as not run
resolution: Remaining gates name it with the other Linux checks.
